## Writer verification with a Siamese network

<!-- Task 3: contrastive or triplet loss; how training examples are constructed; matching performance. -->

A Siamese neural network was trained on the handwriting images and evaluated to assess how accurately it could capture whether two digits were written by the same writer. 

### Pair construction
We controlled for digit identity by constructing pairs consisting of the same digits. Therefore, a positive pair for this network consisted of two different images of the same digit written by the same person, and a negative pair contained two images of the same digit but by different writers. Examples of pairs from the training and validation datasets are shown in @fig-pairs. We employed a balanced pair sampling approach with half of the pairs being positive and the remaining half negative to ensure the Siamese network learned effectively [@chopra_2005].

```{r}
#| label: fig-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Example training and validation pairs. Top row: training pairs (same writer left, different writer right). Bottom row: validation pairs (same writer left, different writer right)."
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 5

par(mfrow = c(2, 4), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))

show_pair <- function(pair_idx, pairs, label) {
  img1 <- x[pairs[pair_idx, 1], , , 1]
  img2 <- x[pairs[pair_idx, 2], , , 1]
  image(t(img1[nrow(img1):1, ]), col = grey(seq(1, 0, length = 256)),
        axes = FALSE, main = label)
  image(t(img2[nrow(img2):1, ]), col = grey(seq(1, 0, length = 256)),
        axes = FALSE, main = "")
}

pos_train <- which(train$y[, 1] == 1)
neg_train <- which(train$y[, 1] == 0)
pos_valid <- which(valid$y[, 1] == 1)
neg_valid <- which(valid$y[, 1] == 0)

show_pair(pos_train[1], train_pairs, "Train: same writer")
show_pair(neg_train[1], train_pairs, "Train: different writer")
show_pair(pos_valid[1], valid_pairs, "Val: same writer")
show_pair(neg_valid[1], valid_pairs, "Val: different writer")
```

### Model structure
We used contrastive loss, introduced by @hadsell_2006, to train the Siamese network. This loss function was chosen over triplet loss because our interest is in distinguishing same-writer from different-writer pairs, rather than learning a relative ranking of dissimilarity between triplets. Additionally, this is a simple binary verification task and the dataset is relatively small. Contrastive loss may therefore be particularly suitable for this setting, given evidence that it can converge faster than triplet loss [@herman_2026]. The contrastive loss for a pair is:

$$
L = yD^2 + (1-y)\max(0,m-D)^2
$$
where $y$ is a binary label with $y$ = 1 for a positive pair (i.e., the same writer and same digit) and $D$ is the Euclidean distance between the embeddings. The hyperparameter $m$ defines the margin: similar pairs incur near-zero loss when their embeddings are close ($d$ is small), while dissimilar pairs incur zero loss only if their distance is at least $m$. This encourages the network to minimise distances between embeddings from the same writer and maximise distances between embeddings from different writers, up to the margin [@Elaraby_2023]. The margin for the initial Siamese network was set to 1, but was optimised in a hyperparameter search.

The shared CNN encoder consisted of two convolutional layers with 16 and 32 filters, respectively, each using a filter size of 3 and a ReLU activation function to introduce non-linearity. A max pooling layer with a pool size and stride of 2 was placed between these convolutional layers. The convolutional layers learn local image features while max pooling reduces the spatial dimensions of the feature maps. The last two layers were a global average pooling layer which converts the feature maps into a vector and a dense layer mapping the vector to a 16-dimensional embedding. A relatively simple encoder is used since the input images are low-resolution and contain features such as curves and strokes that the network can learn from these images.

### Training

In the Siamese model, pairs of images are supplied to the encoder to produce their embeddings and then the Euclidean distance between each pair is calculated. The model was compiled using the Adam optimiser and used the above contrastive loss function which was calculated using the Euclidean distances and a margin of one, and averaged for every batch. The number of epochs was set to 5 and the batch size to 64. 

```{r}
#| label: snn-cache

# After changing any of the training code, delete the files and render again.
snn_original_validation_file <- "results/snn_original_validation.rds"
snn_original_test_file <- "results/snn_original_test.rds"
snn_run <- !file.exists(snn_original_validation_file) || !file.exists(snn_original_test_file) 

```

```{r}
#| label: encoderbuild
#| eval: !expr snn_run

set_random_seed(25) # set random seed for tensorflow

# Build shared encoder - the same as the notes to keep it simple 
image <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1)) # each image = 28x28, 1 image channel

z <- image |>
  layer_conv_2d(16, 3, activation = "relu") |> # learns useful features (shapes, strokes)
  layer_max_pooling_2d(2) |> # makes feature maps smaller while keeping important info
  layer_conv_2d(32, 3, activation = "relu") |>
  layer_global_average_pooling_2d() |> # converts feature maps -> single vector of numbers
  layer_dense(16) # converts to 16-number embedding representing the handwriting style

encoder <- keras_model(image, z)

```

```{r}
#| label: siamesebuild
#| eval: !expr snn_run

# a & b = describes pair of images supplied to model
a <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
b <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))

# encoders produce the embeddings for a & b
# distance calculates the Euclidean distance between their embeddings 
distance <- list(encoder(a), encoder(b)) |>
  layer_lambda(f = function(z) {
    op_sqrt(op_sum(op_square(z[[1]] - z[[2]]), 
                   axis = 2, # sum over embedding dimension
                   keepdims = TRUE) + 
              1e-7) # makes sure it's not 0
  })

# distance = model output
model <- keras_model(list(a, b), distance) 
```

```{r}
#| label: compile
#| eval: !expr snn_run

# Use Adam optimiser to compile model and contrastive loss function defined earlier
model |> compile(
  optimizer = optimizer_adam(1e-3),
  loss = contrastive_loss # using fn from siameseFunctions.R
)

# Fit model with training data and validation data
model |> fit(
  list(train$left, train$right), train$y,
  validation_data = list(
    list(valid$left, valid$right), valid$y
  ),
  epochs = 5,
  batch_size = 64,
  verbose=0
)

# Calculate the model predicted distances between the pairs in the validation data
valid_distance <- as.numeric(predict(model, list(valid$left, valid$right), verbose = 0))

# Calculate the model predicted distances between the pairs in the test data
test_distance <- as.numeric(predict(model, list(test$left, test$right), verbose =0))

saveRDS(valid_distance, snn_original_validation_file)
saveRDS(test_distance, snn_original_test_file)
```

```{r}
#| label: valid_dist

valid_distance <- readRDS(snn_original_validation_file)

# Extract the observed labels for whether the pairs are the same or different for validation data
valid_same <- as.logical(valid$y[, 1])

# Function to calculate balanced accuracy at different thresholds
balanced_accuracy_at <- function(distance, same, cut) {
  predicts_same <- distance < cut # at given threshold (cut) would model predict same or different?
  same_rate <- mean(predicts_same[same]) # accuracy for "same" pairs
  different_rate <- mean(!predicts_same[!same]) # accuracy for "different" pairs
  (same_rate + different_rate) / 2 # mean accuracy for "same" and "different" ("alanced accuracy)
}

threshold_candidates <- sort(unique(valid_distance)) # threshold candidates are based on the distances themselves
threshold_scores <- vapply(threshold_candidates, balanced_accuracy_at, distance = valid_distance, same = valid_same, numeric(1)) # calculate balanced accuracy for all threshold candidates using fn from siameseFunctions.R
threshold <- threshold_candidates[which.max(threshold_scores)] 
best_index <- which.max(threshold_scores) # index for the threshold that maximises the balanced accuracy
threshold <- threshold_candidates[best_index] # threshold that maximises the balanced accuracy
```

We compared the balanced accuracy for same and different digit pairs from the validation set at different Euclidean distance thresholds, and chose the threshold which maximised the balanced accuracy. The different thresholds tested were all the actual distances between the validation pairs. The selected threshold was `r round(threshold, 2)`, giving a validation balanced accuracy of `r round(threshold_scores[best_index]*100, 2)`%. 

### Writer verification performance

The generalisability of our model was evaluated by predicting on unseen writers' digit image-pairs in the test set and calculating the balanced accuracy. Balanced accuracy was also calculated by digit to assess how performance varied for different digits (@tbl-snn-test-digits) and calculated separately for pairs in the same and different sessions to assess how session changes affect performance (@tbl-snn-test-sessions). We did not specify how many of each digit to use nor whether images should be from the same or different sessions when creating pairs of images. Thus, the number of pairs of images of each digit, and whether the pair was from the same session or not were random with ratios related to the proportion of images of each digit (1:1:1:1:1; @tbl-snn-test-digits) and the proportion of images in the same and different sessions in the test set (1:4; @tbl-snn-test-sessions). Examples of test pairs with predicted and true labels are shown in @fig-test-results.

```{r}
#| label: snn-test

test_distance <- readRDS(snn_original_test_file)

# Extract the observed labels for whether the pairs are the same or different for test data
true_same <- as.logical(test$y[, 1]) 

# Calculate balanced accuracy on test set
snn_test_results <- balanced_accuracy_at(distance = test_distance, same = true_same, cut = threshold)

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-snn-test-digits
#| tbl-cap: "Balanced accuracy for Siamese neural network predictions on pairs of images in the test set including a breakdown of balanced accuracy by digit ordered from highest to lowest balanced accuracy."

# Break down balanced accuracy by digit
# Set up tibble for results with the first row the combined balanced accuracy
snn_test_results_table_digits <- tibble(Digit = "All digits", 
                                        Images = length(true_same), 
                                        Balanced_accuracy = snn_test_results)

# Find the digit used in each pair in test_pairs
test_digits <- tibble(image_id = test_pairs[, 1]) %>% 
  left_join(handwriting$metadata) %>% 
  select(digit) %>% pull()

# Add digit to tibble with true and predicted same or different
test_digits_df <- tibble(true_same = true_same,
                         test_distance = test_distance,
                         test_digits = test_digits)

# Loop over each digit and calculate metrics for each then append row to results table
for (i in 0:4) {
  
  test_digits_df_temp <- test_digits_df %>% filter(test_digits == i)
  
  snn_test_results_digits_loop <- balanced_accuracy_at(distance = test_digits_df_temp$test_distance, 
                                           same = test_digits_df_temp$true_same, 
                                           cut = threshold)
  
  snn_test_results_table_digits <- snn_test_results_table_digits %>% add_row(Digit = as.character(i), Images = nrow(test_digits_df_temp), Balanced_accuracy = snn_test_results_digits_loop)
  
}

snn_test_results_table_digits %>%
  mutate(across(c(Balanced_accuracy), ~ 100 * .x)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Balanced_accuracy)) %>%
  arrange(Digit == "All digits") %>%
  kable(digits = 1, align = "r", col.names = c("Digit", "Image pairs", "Test balanced accuracy (%)"))

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-snn-test-sessions
#| tbl-cap: "Balanced accuracy for Siamese neural network predictions on pairs of images in the test set including a breakdown of balanced accuracy for digits in the same and in different sessions."

# Break down balanced accuracy by session
# Set up tibble for results with the first row the combined balanced accuracy
snn_test_results_table_sessions <- tibble(Session = "All sessions", 
                                          Images = length(true_same), 
                                          Balanced_accuracy = snn_test_results)

# Find the session used in each pair in test_pairs for both left and right images
test_session_left <- tibble(image_id = test_pairs[, 1]) %>% 
  left_join(handwriting$metadata) %>% 
  select(session) %>% pull()

test_session_right <- tibble(image_id = test_pairs[, 2]) %>% 
  left_join(handwriting$metadata) %>% 
  select(session) %>% pull()

# Add digit to tibble with true and predicted same or different
test_session_df <- tibble(true_same = true_same,
                         test_distance = test_distance,
                         # session the same or different 
                         test_session = factor(x = test_session_left == test_session_right, 
                                               levels = c(TRUE, FALSE), 
                                               labels = c("Same session", "Different session"))) # change to named factor

# Loop over each digit and calculate metrics for each then append row to results table
for (i in c("Same session", "Different session")) {
  
  test_session_df_temp <- test_session_df %>% filter(test_session == i)
  
  snn_test_results_sessions_loop <- balanced_accuracy_at(distance = test_session_df_temp$test_distance, 
                                           same = test_session_df_temp$true_same, 
                                           cut = threshold)
  
  snn_test_results_table_sessions <- snn_test_results_table_sessions %>% add_row(Session = as.character(i), Images = nrow(test_session_df_temp), Balanced_accuracy = snn_test_results_sessions_loop)
  
}

snn_test_results_table_sessions %>%
  mutate(across(c(Balanced_accuracy), ~ 100 * .x)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Balanced_accuracy)) %>%
  arrange(Session == "All sessions") %>%
  kable(digits = 1, align = "r", col.names = c("Session", "Image pairs", "Test balanced accuracy (%)"))


```

```{r}
#| label: fig-test-results
#| fig-cap: "Sample test pairs with true label, predicted label, and distance score. Green border = correct prediction, red = incorrect."

set.seed(38)
n_show <- 8
sample_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(test_pairs)), n_show)

par(mfrow = c(4, 4), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2.5, 0.5))

for (i in sample_idx) {
  img1 <- x[test_pairs[i, 1], , , 1]
  img2 <- x[test_pairs[i, 2], , , 1]
  
  true_label   <- ifelse(test$y[i, 1] == 1, "Same", "Different")
  pred_label   <- ifelse(test_distance[i] < threshold, "Same", "Different")
  correct      <- true_label == pred_label
  border_col   <- ifelse(correct, "forestgreen", "red3")
  score        <- round(test_distance[i], 3)
  
  title_text <- paste0("True: ", true_label, ",", " Pred: ", pred_label, "\nd = ", score)
  
  # left image
  image(t(img1[nrow(img1):1, ]), col = grey(seq(1, 0, length = 256)),
        axes = FALSE, main = title_text,
        cex.main = 1)
  box(col = border_col, lwd = 2)
  
  # right image
  image(t(img2[nrow(img2):1, ]), col = grey(seq(1, 0, length = 256)),
        axes = FALSE, main = "")
  box(col = border_col, lwd = 2)
}
```
